unit.title: Introduction
unit.needIt: This course helps you understand why you sometimes do things you regret, like scrolling on your phone instead of studying. It gives you tools to manage your impulses and make better choices for your long-term goals.
unit.why: The lecture explores how humans are both rational thinkers and animals driven by instinct. It uses stories like the Ring of Gyges to ask if we are only good because we are afraid of getting caught. It also looks at how we can use simple tricks, like freezing a credit card, to help us stick to our plans.
unit.outcome: Understand the balance between rational choice and instinctual behavior.

quiz.q: What is the main goal of the first part of the lecture?
quiz.why: The speaker says they want to give a broad overview of the course and their goals.
quiz.quote: In the first part of the lecture, I'm just going to a very broad overview of what kind of course this is and to say a few words about what my goals are for the course.

quiz.q: What are the three main ethical theories the course covers?
quiz.why: The lecture explicitly lists these three theories as part of the Western philosophical tradition.
quiz.quote: We'll talk about utilitarianism, we'll talk about deontology, and we'll talk about virtue ethics, and we'll talk about how those relate to one another.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a topic mentioned as part of the course?
quiz.why: The speaker explicitly states that the course is not a course in metaphysics.
quiz.quote: It's not a course in metaphysics. It's not a course in epistemology.

quiz.q: What does the speaker say about the 'Ring of Gyges' story?
choices: It shows we are naturally good
quiz.why: Glaucon argues that people only act morally because they fear the punishment of society.
quiz.quote: They act in that way because they fear the punishment of society. They don't act in that way because it's in any way valuable to them.

quiz.q: What is the 'push the fat man' case used to explore?
quiz.why: The speaker uses these cases to ask if there is a moral difference between different actions.
quiz.quote: What is it that explains the differences in our reactions to these cases?

partials: Humans are also subject to non-reflective forces.
We can plan for the future.
We often fail to act on those plans.
We can use strategies to help ourselves.
crystal.key: Human nature is a mix of rational planning and non-reflective instincts.

decoys.text: The Ring of Gyges proves people are naturally good.
